items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: That's Chris Kelly's band I was playing with then.

ctx.x: It sounds a bit like that blues that I believe Chris Kelly used to play.
That's Chris Kelly's band I was playing with then.

It used to be as funny as the good ones. Yeah. And with that thing that you were humming there, was that the trumpet part? Yeah, that's the starry blues. And I know that it was this blues that they recorded, and of course Chris Kelly never made any records either, but this record that they made in 1943 with Kit Howard. Supposed to have played a little bit like him.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: You know, when you hire Chris Kelly's band you want to see the band... People knew him and knew the band.

ctx.x: And he had Earl Foster singing with him in the picture.

Over in Mandeville. Mandeville, yeah. Well that's where they was, they were bootlegged for back over there. Oh yeah. He made a good reputation over there. After he, Buddy Manity bandit the same as Chris did. Chris had a line of work around the other man, he was working exactly every night. Five nights every week, sometimes every night. Mm-hmm. He take them double dates. Mm-hmm. All right now, you hire him. Play up your own Pine Street, you know, frat house. Mm-hmm. He take that date. He take a date, I tell the…
What did Mealy Barnes play like then, in those days?

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: when you hire Chris Kelly's band, you want to see the band... He's there, all right. Now, he sent us someplace else.

ctx.x: Play up your own Pine Street, you know. Mm-hmm. He take that date. He take a date. Mm-hmm. I tell you, the old one talk, he used to run out there every Friday night. Mm-hmm. That lady used to run that talk out there. Another lady, we have a coffee now. But he had all that. But now, what he do? He take them dates. Sometimes, he have three dates. Why he break his band up?
